title: Wildfire Boundary Polygons from USGS and CalFire in cloud native formats
description: Snapshots of fire polygon boundaries from USGS Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity (MTBS) and the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CalFire), including burned area extents and controlled burn treatments through 2022. Also includes Wildfire Hazard Potential raster data for the contiguous United States at 270-m resolution. Distributed in cloud-native formats including PMTiles and GeoParquet.

## README.md
# fire 

Snapshots of fire polygons data from multiple sources.  Cloud-optimized formats include PMTiles and (Geo)Parquet serializations.

## USGS MTBS Fire perimiters:

- Original shapefiles for burned area extent downloaded from: https://edcintl.cr.usgs.gov/downloads/sciweb1/shared/MTBS_Fire/data/composite_data/burned_area_extent_shapefile/mtbs_perimeter_data.zip

## Calfire 

- Original geodatabase file up to year 2022 downloaded from: https://www.fire.ca.gov/what-we-do/fire-resource-assessment-program/gis-mapping-and-data-analytics

PMTiles created using gdal 3.8.4 via

```
ogr2ogr -dsco MAX_SIZE=50000000 -dsco MAX_FEATURES=20000000 calfire-2022.pmtiles CALFIRE/fire22_1.gdb
```

[Example map](https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fire/fire-pmtiles.html) created using [map.py](https://data.source.coop/cboettig/fire/map.py)

## Wildfire Hazard Potential

> Dillon, Gregory K. 2023. Wildfire Hazard Potential for the United States (270-m), version 2023. 4th Edition. Fort Collins, CO: Forest Service Research Data Archive. https://doi.org/10.2737/RDS-2015-0047-4
